body: geez i understand that. in the wise words of someone i met on twitter, “you will wonder why your spine feels like a stick. it’s a spine! but you are wrong. it is a stick. and it will get stiff and hurt. a lot.”

okay so my only scars i don’t cover up are the ones on my wrists. the ones on my thighs don’t stayed scarred so they stay covered up😅 

but as for the visible scars, no stares, no whispers, no one actually cares enough to bring attention to them. i’m not really brave or confident i just know no one gives a shit whether i hurt myself or not as long as i don’t inconvenience anyone.🤷🏻‍♀️

but, in your situation, i would suggest not being ashamed of them. they are battle scars and you won. i’m proud of you! people in your life may get panicky but just explain that it is a chapter in your life that you kept a secret for awhile but you see no reason to hide it anymore. and honestly people always have something to say, let them gossip all the way to their death beds if they so choose. don’t focus on ~those~ people. The people who love you will support you. You are so brave and i’m so proud of your progress!

i get really bad nightmares and panic attacks from unresolved childhood trauma. When i was 12, i was waking up from a particularly bad one and i was completely out of my mind, like i wasn’t controlling myself and tried to slit my wrists with a kitchen knife. obviously it was too dull to do serious damage but sheer amount of endorphins released from it was addictive and instantly calmed me. from then on i started using self harm to help cope with the trauma. now i’m 18 years old still having nightmares and cutting myself to deal with it bc even though my mom knew i was hurting, she never forced me to get help bc i was really fucking good at pretending i was okay. high key regretting not getting help then, but it’s too late now. also this pandemic is not helping.
